record.context_brief: Entropy functions for sets and measures
record.original_question: For entropy notions of compact sets and probability measures in metric or Hilbert spaces, including H_epsilon, H_{epsilon,delta}, tilde H_epsilon, and tilde H_{epsilon,delta}, what are their properties and how are they related?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\rho)$ be a complete metric space (in particular a separable Hilbert space). For a compact subset $K\subset X$ and $\varepsilon>0$, define the $\varepsilon$-entropy
$$H_\varepsilon(K) := \log_2 N_\varepsilon(K),$$
where $N_\varepsilon(K)$ is the minimal number of closed balls of radius $\varepsilon$ in $X$ needed to cover $K$. For a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $X$ and $\varepsilon,\delta>0$, define the $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-entropy
$$H_{\varepsilon,\delta}(\mu) := \inf\{\log_2 N : \exists \text{ Borel sets } A_1,\dots,A_N \text{ of diameter } \le 2\varepsilon \text{ with } \mu(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_N)\ge 1-\delta\}.$$
Analogously define the "dual" or covering-by-measures versions $\tilde H_\varepsilon(K)$ as $\log_2$ of the minimal cardinality of an $\varepsilon$-net of $K$ (i.e. a finite subset $F\subset K$ such that every point of $K$ is within $\varepsilon$ of $F$), and $\tilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}(\mu)$ as $\log_2$ of the minimal number of points $x_1,\dots,x_N\in X$ such that $\mu(\bigcup_i B(x_i,\varepsilon))\ge 1-\delta$.

Problem. Investigate the properties of the four functionals $H_\varepsilon$, $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$, $\tilde H_\varepsilon$, $\tilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ (monotonicity, continuity, sub/superadditivity, behaviour under push-forward, asymptotics as $\varepsilon,\delta\to 0$, finiteness/infiniteness, dependence on the ambient geometry), and establish the precise quantitative relations between them — in particular inequalities comparing $H_\varepsilon$ with $\tilde H_\varepsilon$ for compact sets, comparisons between $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ and $\tilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ for probability measures, and the connection between the set-entropies and the measure-entropies via supports and weak limits.
artifact.category_tag: metric entropy of sets and measures
artifact.status_search_result: While classical $\varepsilon$-entropy of compact sets (Kolmogorov–Tikhomirov) and $\varepsilon$-entropy of probability distributions (Posner–Rodemich and others) are well-developed, a unified systematic comparison of the four variants $H_\varepsilon, H_{\varepsilon,\delta}, \tilde H_\varepsilon, \tilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ as posed appears to remain an investigative problem; no source found resolves it as a single program.

status_evidence.title: Epsilon-entropy - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: The ε-entropy H_ε(C,X) of a set C in a metric space equals log_2 N_ε(C,X).
status_evidence.claim: Classical definition of H_epsilon exists but the broader comparative study is not consolidated.

status_evidence.title: Epsilon Entropy of Probability Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Epsilon-delta entropy is introduced for probabilistic metric spaces; for ε,δ>0 it is finite, but for δ=0 it can be infinite.
status_evidence.claim: Separate theories for set- and measure-entropies exist; unified properties remain to be investigated.
